title: Loop Iterator Helper Comments
pattern: Comments explaining math calculations inside nested loops using generic, uninformative iterator names (`i`, `j`).
why_bad: Hides business domain concepts. Renaming the iterators to clear domain terms (like `factor`, `multiple`) makes the code self-documenting and removes the need for structural explanations.
detection: Nested loops utilizing single-letter iterators (`i`, `j`, `k`) accompanied by descriptive comments explaining what the math represents.
counterexample: Loops over domain-named iterators (`factor`, `multiple`) that read as self-documenting math without prose.
fix: Rename loop iterators to meaningful domain names and remove the explanatory comment.
source: Steve McConnell, *Code Complete* (2004), Chapter 32 ("Java Example of Poor Documentation Resulting from Bad Programming Style").
